quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. You must be able to stop within the area your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road or pavement edge, you should:

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the roadway when safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the roadway when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not try to turn back onto the road immediately. Instead, slow down, check for traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right before the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, continue through the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians waiting for a "Walk" signal on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: A red traffic light is showing, but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions. An officer's instructions override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead.
Side Road.
Railroad Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a stop sign is coming ahead.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into the first lane.
Turn into the second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. If you are under 21 and any amount of alcohol is found in your blood, your license will be suspended for two years.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes direction or becomes narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road changes direction or becomes narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is about to change direction or get narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On expressways with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic around you, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Which of these roads is most likely to be slippery after snow or rain in cold weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A shaded road

questions.correctAnswerText: A shaded road
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze first and melt last. On cold, wet days, shaded parts of the road are more likely to be icy than sunny areas.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route to your destination.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to the correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on the freeway road or shoulder. Continue driving to the next exit or crossroad instead. Other drivers will not expect you to back up, and this can cause a crash.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other car.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough space. Before moving back to your lane, make sure you have enough room between you and the car you passed. You can return to the right lane safely when both headlights of the other car are visible in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear is skidding left, steer left. This will straighten out your car.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as normal traffic fines.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to slow down or stop for equipment. Driving carefully in work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NEVER:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder and watch for drivers trying to enter your lane. Never pass or change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light ahead. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass before the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means you should prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, leave it quickly.

questions.question: You are exiting the interstate. When should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When a bicyclist turns left, what may they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut across all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You may see a bicyclist in the left lane when turning.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass any vehicles that appear to be stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic lines meet, look both left and right to make sure nothing is coming.
